issue.title: just test-visual is 360/840 red on clean master: a one-row chrome shift was rebaselined into only some goldens
issue.description:
`just test-visual` on a clean master tree fails 360 of 840 PNG goldens. The lane is
excluded from `just test`/`just check`/`just check-full` (`FAST_MARKER_EXPRESSION =
"not slow and not visual"` in `tools/run_pytest`), so every recent landing has been
green without anyone running it, and the corpus has drifted a long way from master.

Measured 2026-08-27 at a7b702863 with a clean tree:

    just test-visual
    ==== 360 failed, 480 passed, 1 skipped in 333.80s (0:05:33) ====

This is not renderer or font drift. The failures cluster on an identical
`changed_pixels: 5181` across many unrelated goldens, and the diff region is confined
to the app chrome behind whatever the test is snapshotting. Comparing actual against
expected for
`test_ace_png_snapshots_config_center_config.py::test_config_center_config_empty_png_snapshot`
shows the background pane content shifted down by exactly one row, with the
right-hand indicator column gaining a row's worth of text -- the signature of a chrome
row added on master whose rebaseline covered only the goldens the adding change
happened to look at.

The likely source is one of the Artifacts chrome rows landed on 2026-08-26, most
plausibly the pane description brief (`ceaa377fe feat(artifacts): add the pane
description brief`), but the audit should confirm that rather than assume it: a
one-row shift is also what a tab-strip or filter-bar row would produce.

## Why this needs judgment, not a blanket `--sase-update-visual-snapshots`

Accepting 360 goldens in one sweep would bless any genuine regression hiding among
them. The work is to identify the chrome change(s) responsible, confirm the shift is
intended, and rebaseline only the goldens that shift for that reason -- then look at
whatever is left over.

## Related, not duplicate

- `bead:sase-sl` corrects the *documentation* of the PNG tolerance (CI uses exact
  comparison with 0 allowed pixels, so these 360 would be red in CI too, not absorbed
  by a ratio tolerance). It does not touch the corpus.
- `bead:sase-ue` / `bead:sase-ui` cover a collection ImportError in one visual file.
- `bead:sase-u4` and `bead:sase-sz` cover timeouts and setup errors in the visual lane
  under load, not golden mismatches.

## Reproduce

    just test-visual
    # then inspect .pytest_cache/sase-visual/<node>/<golden>/{summary.txt,diff.png}

FOUND BY the `sase-ug` land agent while adding the link-rail PNG goldens that epic's
`rail` phase never shipped. Nothing in `sase-ug` causes this: the failures reproduce
with the epic's only source change stashed, and stale artifacts already in
`.pytest_cache/sase-visual/` carry the same signature dated 2026-08-23, three days
before the epic began.

task_type_fields.why_not_flake: Deterministic, not intermittent: 360 of 840 goldens fail on every run of a clean tree, many with a byte-identical changed_pixels: 5181, and the diff is a structural one-row shift of the app chrome rather than antialiasing noise. Reruns reproduce the same set. The lane is excluded from just check/check-full, so this accumulated unnoticed rather than appearing under load.

payload.entry:
RE-MEASURED 2026-08-27 at master 259f39901 (12 commits after the a7b702863 measurement in this bead's description): the lane is now 839 passed / 1 failed / 1 skipped in 232s, not 480/840. Master's eaf4ea891 ('route Artifacts digit presses through the live seam and rebaseline PNG goldens', sase-um.5.1.2) regenerated the corpus and cleared 359 of the 360 failures this bead reported, so the one-row chrome-shift backlog described above is DISCHARGED.

ONE golden still fails, with a DIFFERENT root cause than the one-row shift:

    tests/ace/tui/visual/test_ace_png_snapshots_agents.py::test_agent_output_variables_multi_agent_png_snapshot
    golden: tests/ace/tui/visual/snapshots/png/agents_output_variables_multi_agent_120x40.png
    changed_pixels: 366 / 1520532 (0.024%), expected_size == actual_size (1482x1026)

The diff is three small glyphs, not a shifted region, and the rendered actual.svg contains no standalone 'q' token anywhere. The golden still carries the retired 'q' asker suffix that 777e51e73 ('feat(agents): retire q asker suffix', sase-ud.12) removed from the render; the bulk regen in eaf4ea891 missed this file, whose last content change was 1f21c4b84. Fix is a single targeted regeneration with --sase-update-visual-snapshots after confirming the three glyph sites are exactly the dropped suffix.

NOT caused by epic sase-ug (the link rail). Verified by stashing the entire sase-ug landing tree (git stash push -u) and reproducing the same single failure on a clean master 259f39901 checkout, then restoring. Also verified the converse: with the sase-ug tree applied, the lane is the same 839/1/1 and the 7 new link_rail_*.png goldens pass, so the app-level Link Rail chrome does not disturb the freshly rebaselined corpus.

SIZE: this bead was sized 'large' against a 360-golden backlog. The remaining work is one golden; the owner may want to re-size it to small when triaging.

Epic sase-um phase sase-um.5.1.2 (eaf4ea891) already absorbed the bulk of this bead: it routed every hard-coded Artifacts digit press through AcePage.artifacts_digit across 71 visual test files, then regenerated 357 goldens after tracing each diff to the agents-first subtab reorder (4dd299502) and the app-level Link Rail (d8e8b5ab8 / a7b702863) rather than accepting them blind. Scope left: Full CI run 33167273442 (2026-08-28) reports only 3 visual-test failures, not 360 -- test_ace_png_snapshots_help_panel.py::test_help_panel_keymaps_png_snapshot, test_ace_png_snapshots_plan_toast.py::test_epic_plan_toast_png_snapshot, and test_ace_png_snapshots_update_toast.py::test_startup_update_toast_png_snapshot. Those three are being carried as remaining sase-um epic work because they keep the heavy lane red and therefore hold the v0.17.0 release shut through ci_watch's heavy_lane_not_green condition. Re-measure this bead's 360/840 claim against current master before working it.

payload.description: Ruled out as the cause here: sase-up is a one-row chrome shift across 360 goldens, while this mismatch keeps the same layout and hit 1 of 841 visual tests.

payload.close_reason: Superseded by sase-x5, which owns the CURRENT residual visual corpus. sase-up's own 2026-08-28 note records that eaf4ea891 traced the chrome/subtab changes and regenerated 357 goldens, reducing the original 360-failure incident to three remaining CI failures. The newer sase-x5 remeasured clean master on 2026-09-05 and isolated 27 repeatable failures among 29 reported, with small per-golden deltas rather than the old uniform 5,181-pixel chrome shift. Keep that newer measured task open; launching a worker against this obsolete 360/840 diagnosis would duplicate and misdirect the remaining work.
